Implementation Plan

I have what I need for the plan. The fix has two parts:

- Implement the `AI_ENGINE_READ_ONLY` narrowing that the tests already expect.
- Drop Bash from the shared `read` profile.

One prompt, the security-pass exhaustion judge, tells the model to run `git`, so it needs a small no-shell fallback line.

Planning ref: `claude/replace-claude-sessions-phase-5c` @ `e9ea390e5dab0ec20c5170c1a7b1614157a6c096`. This matches the integration branch metadata (`Integration branch mismatch: false`).

Scope-mode: Hold Scope
Reuse-audit: extends READ_PROFILE_ALLOW / PROFILE_TOOLS / resolve() in scripts/claude_engine.py and claude_run in scripts/ai_engine.sh
Scope-mode justification: The answers (Q1: A, Q2: A) set the scope: remove Bash from the shared Claude `read` profile so every read role (CLARIFY, CLARIFY_RESPOND, SECURITY_JUDGE, SECURITY_AUDIT, WORKFLOW_HEAL) loses shell access, and make the RB_JUDGE verdict pass actually run with that profile. While planning I found that `AI_ENGINE_READ_ONLY` is set by `scripts/review_rb_judge.sh:113` but never read by `scripts/ai_engine.sh` or `scripts/claude_engine.py`. So today the RB_JUDGE verdict pass on Claude resolves to the `write` profile (`bypassPermissions`, with Edit/Write/WebFetch/WebSearch). That is worse than the audit finding describes. `tests/test_ai_engine.py::test_read_only_switch_narrows_a_write_role` (lines 302-311) already expects the narrowing, so that test fails on this ref. Under Boil the Lake, a one-line, engine-neutral no-shell fallback goes into the exhaustion-judge prompt (and its template twin). SECURITY_JUDGE runs on Claude by default, and that prompt tells the model to run `git log`/`git diff`. This adds well under 30 LOC and no new dependency or interface, so completeness wins (§6: Security > Correctness & safety > Backward compatibility > Operational clarity > Performance > Speed). Container isolation (Q1: B/C) is out of scope.

Automation / §20 surface:
- New script: none. This only changes existing code (`scripts/claude_engine.py`, `scripts/ai_engine.sh`, two prompt files, tests, README, a changelog fragment).
- Scheduler / PR-push entry point: no new wiring. The change takes effect through the existing callers: `review_autofix.yml`, which runs `scripts/review_rb_judge.sh` → `review_rb_claude_run read`; `orchestrate_poll.yml`, which runs `scripts/orchestrate_poll_process.sh` → `poller_claude_judge`; and the clarify / heal / security-audit paths that call `claude_run`. CI runs the tests through the existing `.github/workflows/ci.yml` test jobs.
- Long-running supervisor: none required.
- DB work: none.
- `docs/scripts-pending-removal.md`: no entry, because no script is added.

Conflicts between the issue and the codebase:
1. The issue says the read profile permits `git show*`. That is true: `READ_PROFILE_ALLOW` in `scripts/claude_engine.py:152-166`, with `PROFILE_TOOLS["read"] = "Read,Grep,Glob,Bash"` at 167-170. But the call it cites, `scripts/review_rb_judge.sh:1469` (`review_rb_claude_run read …`), does not get the read profile at all today:
   - `review_rb_claude_run` (lines 104-116) exports `AI_ENGINE_READ_ONLY=true`.
   - `claude_run` in `scripts/ai_engine.sh:196-203` takes `profile` only from `claude_engine.py resolve`.
   - `resolve()` (`claude_engine.py` around 375-431) returns `defaults["profile"]`, which is `write` for RB_JUDGE (`.github/ai/claude_engine.json`).
   - Net effect: the verdict pass currently runs with Edit/Write and `bypassPermissions`. Both defects are fixed here.
2. `README.md:1891-1893` already claims the verdict pass runs with the read-only profile (`AI_ENGINE_READ_ONLY=true`). That is false today and becomes true after this change.

1. Files likely to change
- `scripts/claude_engine.py`
  - `READ_PROFILE_ALLOW` (lines 150-166): reduce to `("Read", "Grep", "Glob")` and rewrite the comment above it. Read roles get no shell, and the reason is that Bash prefix rules are not a write boundary (`git show --output=<file>`, `git diff --output`, `git log --output` all write files).
  - `PROFILE_TOOLS["read"]` (line 169): `"Read,Grep,Glob"`.
  - `resolve()` (around line 428): narrow-only override. When `env.get("AI_ENGINE_READ_ONLY", "").strip() == "true"`, set `profile = "read"`. Never widen: any other value keeps `defaults["profile"]`, and a role whose default is `read` stays `read`. Update the docstring.
  - Check that the `resolve` CLI subcommand passes `os.environ` (or an equivalent mapping) into `resolve()`. If it builds a filtered env, add `AI_ENGINE_READ_ONLY` to it.
- `scripts/ai_engine.sh`
  - `claude_run`, the `case "${profile}"` block (lines 236-241): `read) tools="Read,Grep,Glob"; mode="dontAsk" ;;`, kept identical to `PROFILE_TOOLS["read"]`, which `tests/test_ai_engine.py:325` pins.
  - Defence in depth, right after `profile=` (line 203): if `AI_ENGINE_READ_ONLY` is exactly `true` and `profile` is not `read`, force `profile=read`. This keeps the read-only guarantee even if a future config or `resolve` change drops it. It is narrow-only and never turns `read` into `write`.
  - Add a short comment naming the env var and its narrow-only contract.
- `prompts/mode-judge-security-pass-exhaustion.txt` and `prompts/_templates/mode-judge-security-pass-exhaustion.txt`: after the line-21 sentence ("…run `git log` / `git diff …`…"), add one engine-neutral sentence. It tells the model that if no shell tool is available, it should verify each finding by reading and searching the cited files in the checkout (the audited head), and must not fail or return an invalid verdict because `git` cannot be run. Make the same addition to the template twin so prompt assembly stays in sync.
- `tests/test_ai_engine.py`
  - Line 297, `test_read_role_command_line`: expect `"Read,Grep,Glob"`.
  - Lines 302-306, parametrize for `test_read_only_switch_narrows_a_write_role`: the `"true"` row expects `("Read,Grep,Glob", "dontAsk")`. The `"false"` and `"yes"` rows keep the write profile.
  - New tests (see section 6).
- `tests/test_review_autofix_claude_fixer_mode.py`: no change expected. Around line 517 it already asserts that `AI_ENGINE_READ_ONLY` is `true` for the `read` access and `false` for `write`. Run it to confirm.
- `README.md`, "Claude engine" section (around lines 1887-1893): one sentence saying the read profile is `Read,Grep,Glob` with no shell (`dontAsk`), that `AI_ENGINE_READ_ONLY=true` narrows any role to it, and that it never widens.
- `changelog.d/6238-claude-read-profile-no-shell.md`, a new fragment per CLAUDE.md §20. The issue number is inferred from the AI memory record for this issue; the implementer should confirm it against the issue being implemented and rename the file if it differs.
- Not touched: `.codex-workflow-src/**` (staged support copy), `scripts/clarify_isolated_run.sh` (already hard-codes `--tools Read,Grep,Glob --permission-mode dontAsk` at line 184, so it is already consistent), `scripts/claude_settings.json.tmpl` (the Bash `PreToolUse` guard hook stays as-is; it simply never fires for read roles), `.github/ai/claude_engine.json` (RB_JUDGE keeps default `write` for the fix pass).

2. Functions or modules to implement
- `claude_engine.resolve(role, config, env, model_hint, effort_hint)`: add the narrow-only `AI_ENGINE_READ_ONLY` handling. Optionally append `"profile narrowed to read by AI_ENGINE_READ_ONLY"` to `warnings`, but only if the existing `AI_ENGINE_SELECTED` logging tolerates extra warnings. Otherwise keep it silent.
- `claude_run` in `scripts/ai_engine.sh`: the defensive narrow plus the new read tool list.
- No new functions.

3. Data structures affected
- `READ_PROFILE_ALLOW` tuple: reduced to `("Read", "Grep", "Glob")`.
- `PROFILE_TOOLS["read"]` string: `"Read,Grep,Glob"`.
- `resolve()` output JSON: same keys, but `profile` can now be `read` for a write-default role when `AI_ENGINE_READ_ONLY=true`.
- The generated `claude-settings.json` for read roles: `permissions.allow` becomes `["Read","Grep","Glob"]`. `deny`, `hooks` and `env` are unchanged.

4. API / interface changes
- Env var `AI_ENGINE_READ_ONLY`: the existing name, already exported by `scripts/review_rb_judge.sh:113`, is now honoured. Only the exact value `true` narrows the profile. Unset, empty or anything else means no change. There is no default value, and that is safe because unset means no change.
- Claude read profile: Bash is removed for CLARIFY, CLARIFY_RESPOND, SECURITY_JUDGE, SECURITY_AUDIT, WORKFLOW_HEAL and the RB_JUDGE verdict pass. Codex and OpenCode paths are unchanged.
- No CLI flag, log prefix, label or JSON field is renamed (§10).

## Decisions

### D1 — Enforce read-only by removing Bash rather than by prefix rules
- Chosen: the Claude `read` profile becomes `--tools Read,Grep,Glob --permission-mode dontAsk` with `allow = ["Read","Grep","Glob"]`, and no `Bash(...)` rules.
- Alternatives considered: tightening the Bash prefix list (for example, denying `*--output*`); running verdict passes in an OS-enforced read-only container like `scripts/clarify_isolated_run.sh` (Q1: B); doing both (Q1: C).
- Why: Q1 was answered A. Prefix rules cannot reliably block git's many file-writing options (`--output`, `-o`, aliases, `-c` config injection), so removing the tool is the only sound fix without a container. The RB_JUDGE verdict prompt already embeds the PR diff and context, and the read-only clarify container already runs with exactly `Read,Grep,Glob`.

### D2 — Apply the hardening to the shared `read` profile, not a new RB_JUDGE-only profile
- Chosen: change `READ_PROFILE_ALLOW` / `PROFILE_TOOLS["read"]` for every read role.
- Alternatives considered: a new stricter profile used only by the RB_JUDGE verdict pass, leaving other read roles on Bash (Q2: B).
- Why: Q2 was answered A. SECURITY_JUDGE (Claude by default) also reads untrusted integration-branch content on the host, and SECURITY_AUDIT and WORKFLOW_HEAL become exposed whenever they are switched to Claude.
